name: EasyTrade - Customer Segmentation & Partner Program Analysis

sections.markdown:
# 👥 EasyTrade — Customer Segmentation & Partner Program Analysis
*7-day review of the customer base by subscription tier, whether tier reflects actual trading behavior, and how the partner offer program is performing.*

## Customer Base by Package Tier
How the active customer base splits across the 3 subscription package tiers.

## Upsell Opportunity — Does Tier Predict Activity?
If higher tiers traded meaningfully more, that would justify tier-based upsell campaigns. **They don't** — average trading volume per trader is essentially flat across all 3 tiers (~$320K–$339K per trader). Package tier is not currently a useful proxy for trading engagement, which suggests upsell targeting should be based on actual activity data instead of the tier a customer happens to be on.

sections.title: Trading Volume & Avg. Volume per Trader by Tier

sections.markdown:
## Partner Offer Program
EasyTrade surfaces cross-sell offers from 5 partner brands. Engagement is currently distributed almost perfectly evenly across all 5 (~510 views each) — the offer-serving logic shows no partner bias.

input.value:
fetch bizevents, from:-7d
| filter event.type == "com.easytrade.offer"
| fieldsAdd partner = arrayElement(splitString(event.category, "/"), 3)
| summarize views = count(), by:{partner}
| sort views desc

sections.markdown:
## Partner Program Trend Over Time
Offer views over time by partner — flat, parallel lines would confirm the even-rotation logic is holding steady rather than drifting toward any one partner.

input.value:
fetch bizevents, from:-7d
| filter event.type == "com.easytrade.offer"
| fieldsAdd partner = arrayElement(splitString(event.category, "/"), 3)
| makeTimeseries views = count(), interval:12h, by:{partner}

sections.markdown:
## Customer Engagement Cadence
Daily count of distinct accounts logging in — the platform's day-to-day active user trend.

input.value:
fetch bizevents, from:-7d
| filter event.type == "com.easytrade.login"
| makeTimeseries active_accounts = countDistinct(accountId), interval:1d
